Our (mirror) repositories hosted on GitHub can be changed so that the risk of people confusing them with real, active repositories is reduced. As such, I propose to follow this checklist for each of [the repositories in the Veloren organization on GitHub](https://github.com/orgs/veloren/repositories), whenever possible: 1. [x] Disable all features in general repository settings except Sponsorships. 2. [x] Update description of repository to include URL of the corresponding source repository on GitLab. 3. [x] Create a workflow under `.github/workflows` so that pull requests are automatically closed and a comment with a reference to the repository on GitLab is created. ## Notes Steps 1 and 2 may be done on GitHub's web UI, while step 3 can be done with a MR on GitLab. ### Step 1 The URL where the features are configured follows this format: `https://github.com/veloren/(repository_name)/settings` Screenshot of how the feature settings would look in the project settings:
Click me
### Step 2 I would change the whole description of each repository with this template: ```txt Mirror of https://gitlab.com/veloren/(repository_name) ``` This way, it should be more clear the repository on GitHub is just that, a mirror. ### Step 3 It may be accomplished globally with the kind of change introduced in this PR:
title: Configure repositories hosted on GitHub

The text for the potion is apparently not correctly generated from fluent parts.

The `buff-agility' string:

~~~
Agility
.desc = Your movement is faster, but you deal less damage, and take more damage.
.stat =
Increases movement speed by { $strength } %.
In return, your attack power and defense decrease drastically.
~~~

is extended with `buff-text-for_seconds`:

~~~
for { $dur_secs } seconds
~~~

Which results in broken text like:

> In return, your attack power and defense decrease drastically.for 25 seconds

See the screenshot:

![image](/uploads/0f678bdf3153c1a02d34e819ab5bd9fb/image.png)
title: Broken string concatenation for potion strings

Veloren HEAD can't be compiled since the update from dependencies yesterday, because the shaderc-sys package uses a deprecated module/syntax of the CMake files from before version 3.5.

OS: ArchLinux
CMake version: 4.0.1
RustC versions: 1.86.0 (2025-02-13) and later


```bash

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `/home/cookiengineer/Software/veloren/veloren/target/release/build/shaderc-sys-ff6c113a5b6c5f26/build-script-build` (exit status: 101)
  --- stdout

  -- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!

  --- stderr
  CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:6 (cmake_minimum_required):
    Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.

    Update the VERSION argument <min> value.  Or, use the <min>...<max> syntax
    to tell CMake that the project requires at least <min> but has been updated
    to work with policies introduced by <max> or earlier.

    Or, add -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 to try configuring anyway.



  thread 'main' panicked at /home/cookiengineer/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/cmake-0.1.54/src/lib.rs:1119:5:

  command did not execute successfully, got: exit status: 1

  build script failed, must exit now
  note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
warning: build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish...
```

When taking a look at the generated `build-script-build` file it seems that it's sourced from this CMake file which is from cmake 2.8 (6 years old):

- https://github.com/pythonesque/shaderc-rs/blob/main/shaderc-sys/build/CMakeLists.txt

I wanted to point out that there's also a fork maintained by google, as it seems, which has the same problem (I tried it with that one, too). Someone has to step up to maintain shaderc-sys, as it seems, because even the google fork isn't really maintained much:

- https://github.com/google/shaderc-rs/tree/main/shaderc-sys/build


What probably needs to be modified is the `build.rs` or the CMakeLists.txt directly. As the warning says, `-DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` is the recommended _temporary_ fix, but it would be better to migrate the dependencies to cmake3.5+ compatible syntaxes.
title: Crate dependency shaderc-sys isn't compatible with CMake >= 4.0.1
